title: Common Errors
markdown:
| Message or symptom | Usual cause | Fix | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IndentationError: expected an indented block` | Nothing indented after a line ending with `:` | Indent the body (4 spaces) | 1.05 |
| `IndentationError: unindent does not match` / `TabError` | Mixed tabs and spaces, or inconsistent indentation | Let the editor insert spaces; re-indent the block | 1.05 |
| `SyntaxError: invalid syntax` at `if x = 5:` | `=` used for comparison | `==` | 1.05 |
| `SyntaxError: '(' was never closed` | A missing bracket, often on the line **before** the error | Check brackets and quotes on the previous lines | 1.01 |
| `TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str` | Adding text and a number | `str(n)`, or an f-string | 1.02 |
| `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'` | `input()` used as a number | `int(input())` | 1.03 |
| The input `5` doubled prints `55` | Multiplying the text from `input` | Convert with `int()` first | 1.03 |
| `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is `False` | Floats are approximate | `math.isclose`, or whole cents | 1.04 |
| `if x == 1 or 2:` is always true | `or 2` is on its own and truthy | `if x in (1, 2):` | 1.05 |
| `IndexError: list index out of range` | Index past the end (remember the last is `len - 1`) | Check the length; use `for item in xs` | 2.02 |
| Changing one list changes another | Two names for the same list, or `[[0] * 3] * 2` | `copy()`, or a comprehension for nested lists | 2.02 |
| `KeyError: 'name'` | Missing dictionary key | `d.get(key, default)`, or `in` first | 2.05 |
| A function's default list keeps old items | Mutable default argument | `None` default, new list inside | 3.02 |
| `UnboundLocalError` | Assigning to a name that is also read in the function before the assignment | Pass it in and return it; `global`/`nonlocal` only if really needed | 3.03 |
| `NameError: name 'x' is not defined` | Typo, or used before it was assigned or imported | Check spelling and order | 3.01 |
| A function prints `None` | No `return` (or printing instead of returning) | `return` the value | 3.01 |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` | Package not installed in this environment, or a typo | `pip install ...` in the active virtual environment | 3.04 |
| Your module behaves strangely on import | Your file is named like a standard module (`random.py`) | Rename the file | 3.04 |
| `FileNotFoundError` | Wrong path, or relative to a different working folder | `Path(__file__).parent / name`, check `exists()` | 3.05 |
| `UnicodeDecodeError` reading a file | Wrong or default encoding | `encoding="utf-8"` (or the file's real encoding) | 3.05 |
| `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute ...` | A function returned `None` (for example `xs.sort()`) | `sorted(xs)`, or check for `None` | 2.02, 4.05 |
| `TypeError: __init__() missing 1 required positional argument` | Creating an object without all arguments, or forgetting `self` | Pass the arguments; `def method(self, ...)` | 4.01 |
| `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` | A list used as a dict key or set item | Use a tuple | 2.04 |
| A generator gives nothing the second time | Generators can be iterated once | Convert to a list, or create it again | 5.02 |
| `itertools.groupby` splits groups | Data not sorted by the group key | Sort by the same key first | 5.04 |
| `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` | Invalid JSON (trailing comma, single quotes) | Fix the data; the message gives line and column | 6.02 |
| CSV fields split wrongly | Splitting lines by hand | Use the `csv` module | 6.02 |
| A regular expression matches too much | Greedy `.*` | `.*?`, or a narrower character class | 6.01 |
